findings.title: Assistant accepts an Event under a Limited Command and ungranted Special Abilities attached to Events
findings.known_status: Newly confirmed prior unverified lead in FE-NOPRUNING. Never part of the original 50 confirmed findings.
findings.source: The second Eligible faction after a Command-only action may take only a Limited Command. Limited Commands have no Special Ability. Ordinary Events can grant only the actions their text specifies.
findings.root_cause: The validator checks that the outer action label is offered but never binds the inner executable plan to that action. The Event early return also bypasses the prohibition on an accompanying ungranted SA.
findings.normal_reproduction: Run probe_durable_action_kind.py. Ordinary llm_seat init/play/submit, Great Revolt seed46 as Belgae. Answer opening non-turn requests with explicit default. The normal Roman bot has taken Command-only, so d000002 offers limited_command/pass. Submit limited_command with player_action.command=Event and event_params.target_region=Provincia.
findings.expected: Reject the plan and keep d000002 pending with the board, Resources, RNG and eligibility unchanged.
findings.observed: The submission is committed as limited_command but executes Ambacti, adding six Roman Auxilia in Provincia (6→12). The same validator accepts Event16 with a standalone Scout, which moves an additional Auxilia from Provincia to Sequani even though the card grants no Scout.
findings.comparator: lod_ai/llm/harness.py:109–111 delegates to the terminal _human_decider. lod_ai/interactive_cli.py:1295–1320 builds actions from the current allowed contract and branches the executable plan from that selected action. This motivated checking the FS typed label/plan binding.
findings.repair_scope: Validate action label, executable Command kind, and SA presence together at the durable and normal SoP boundary. Keep Event-granted actions governed by their separate grant requests. Cover Event-as-Limited-Command, Command-only-with-SA, and Event-plus-ungranted-SA in one repair.
findings.comparison_pattern: lod_ai/llm/harness.py:109–111 delegates to the terminal _human_decider. lod_ai/interactive_cli.py:1295–1320 builds actions from the current allowed contract and branches the executable plan from that selected action. This motivated checking the FS typed label/plan binding.
findings.prior_status: Newly confirmed prior unverified lead in FE-NOPRUNING. Never part of the original 50 confirmed findings.
findings.disposition: The offered action and executable plan agree in the assistant and ordinary turn executor. Event grants use their scoped requests. The normal assistant session preserves the pending decision and replays a corrected response.

findings.title: Assistant Event submissions can execute any supplied card ID instead of the current Event
findings.known_status: New confirmed finding outside the original 50.
findings.rule: Chapter 2 §2.3.4, Event shown on the card; Chapter 5 §5.1
findings.source: An eligible faction choosing Event executes the Event shown on the current card.
findings.root_cause: Human Event execution trusts details.card_id over state.current_card. The durable validator never checks that they identify the current card under the saved edition.
findings.normal_reproduction: Run probe_durable_card_identity.py. Ordinary llm_seat init/play/submit, Great Revolt seed46 as Romans, opening current card16. Submit event with player_action.command=Event and details.card_id=13. No board/save editing is needed.
findings.expected: Reject card13 while card16 is current and retain the same pending decision, or resolve only the current card when redundant identity is absent.
findings.observed: The submission commits a turn recorded against card16, but applies card13 Balearic Slingers and installs capability13 Unshaded. It then advances normally.
findings.comparator: lod_ai/interactive_cli.py:1341–1350 closes the Event runner over the current card argument and invokes engine.handle_event with that card. The LLM bridge answers the existing menu and cannot replace the card object.
findings.repair_scope: Bind human SoP Event identity to the current card while preserving intentional internal card dispatch and effective original/revised aliases. Add stale/off-card, cross-scenario and edition-aware acceptance tests.

findings.title: A shadow command_parts list lets a Limited Command execute in multiple Regions
findings.expected: A Limited Command selects just one Region. Extra inactive representations of a Command must be rejected or excluded from its legality calculation.
findings.observed: The durable assistant accepts a Limited Recruit whose real recruit_plan names Provincia and Sequani when command_parts contains a single Provincia-only Recruit. It commits one new Auxilia to each Region and records the supplied plan in the decision log. Without the shadow command_parts field, the same two-Region plan is rejected.
findings.cause: command_parts(action) returns the supplied list regardless of whether the executor will use it. The limited-region validator examines that list. The one-entry list avoids the len(parts)>1 structural checks. Ordinary non-during execution instead executes the outer plan.
findings.normal_entry_witness: probe_shadow_parts.py creates a scenario-derived legal board and resolves the first Arverni Command through play_card, obtaining a real second-Eligible Roman Limited Command window. It then uses cmd_play/cmd_submit, closes the offered timing decisions, and loads the committed save with validate=True.
findings.comparison_pattern: Liberty or Death checks actual affected spaces after sandbox execution and before committing a Limited Command. Its historical Muster bug demonstrated why checking one authored subplan does not establish the final Command's scope.
findings.prior_status: New confirmed ordinary Sequence-of-Play gap. Related shadow-plan guards already exist for special Event grants and Seize, including test_roman_event_grants.py:339 and test_seize_tribes.py:95-105. The general Limited Command validator still accepts the shape. This is distinct from repeated Battle Region execution and outer action-label mismatches.
findings.repair_scope: Make the structural parser and executor share the same active Command representation. Reject command_parts outside a valid two-part during-Command structure, and validate each actual executable part. Preserve the Limited Command action type through all durable and raw execution entry points.
findings.regression_gate: The witness should become a rejected-input regression. The pending request, board, RNG, accepted journal and log must remain unchanged after rejection. Cover ordinary Limited Recruit, Rally and March or Battle plus valid two-part interruption behavior.
findings.disposition: Only an active two-portion interruption can supply command_parts. Both portions use the same Command and cannot contain nested interruptions. A shadow Recruit list no longer conceals a second Region.

findings.title: Ordinary Battle accepts repeated Regions and the attacker as its own defender
findings.known_status: New confirmed extension beyond the closed Seize/Entreat repetition finding. Duplicate and opposing-Faction checks currently exist only for the sa_after_step Battle form.
findings.expected: A Command selects a Region only once and Battles exactly one opposing Faction there. Durable human input must reject repeated Battle Regions and self-targets before accepting a turn.
findings.observed: A Limited Command with two Carnutes Battle entries, one against Arverni and one against Aedui, passes durable validation and executes two Battles, removing both defending Warbands. The legal one-entry control removes only the first defender. A separate Battle targeting the attacking Romans passes validation and reduces four Roman Auxilia to one by fighting themselves.
findings.comparison: Liberty or Death coin-implementation-lessons.md §E describes repeated per-Command effects and stresses a shared execution-wide guard. Its British MUSTER case also tests the actual aggregate action beyond the planner's first selection. Falling Sky validates duplicate Battle Regions only on an interrupted variant.
findings.repair_scope: Share Battle Region/defender validation across ordinary and interrupted human Battle plans. Preserve separately scoped trusted Event queues where repeated visits can represent distinct granted Commands. Add acceptance/rollback tests for ordinary and Limited input.
findings.comparison_pattern: Liberty or Death coin-implementation-lessons.md §E describes repeated per-Command effects and stresses a shared execution-wide guard. Its British MUSTER case also tests the actual aggregate action beyond the planner's first selection. Falling Sky validates duplicate Battle Regions only on an interrupted variant.
findings.prior_status: New confirmed extension beyond the closed Seize/Entreat repetition finding. Duplicate and opposing-Faction checks currently exist only for the sa_after_step Battle form.
findings.disposition: Ordinary and interrupted human Battle share Region and defender checks. One opposing Faction may defend in each selected Region, including when the plan uses ranked targets.

findings.title: Alternate March forms bypass Limited Command and Britannia restrictions
findings.known_status: New confirmed normalization gap. Both origins/routes and alternate accepted plan representations reach the public human executor.
findings.expected: The one-origin Limited March and Britannia Special Ability prohibition must apply to every accepted March representation. Extra groups must use selected origins.
findings.observed: A Limited March moves Aedui Warbands from Carnutes to Veneti and Mandubii to Treveri and pays for both origins when encoded as explicit_moves or with an undeclared extra_groups origin. Equivalent canonical two-origin input is rejected. An explicit_moves March from Britannia to Morini then executes Trade for six Resources, while the equivalent origins/routes plan is rejected under §4.1.3.
findings.comparison: Liberty or Death coin-implementation-lessons.md §B covers data-shape mismatches and §E records a Limited MUSTER cap bypass when a later phase adds another space. The same aggregate-footprint check is missing for Falling Sky's alternate March shapes.
findings.repair_scope: Normalize accepted March plans before applying structural rules, or reject unsupported human aliases. Include extra-group origins and every explicit path in the same Limited/Britannia validation. Preserve internal Event grants and legacy bot inputs through their explicit trusted entry points.
findings.comparison_pattern: Liberty or Death coin-implementation-lessons.md §B covers data-shape mismatches and §E records a Limited MUSTER cap bypass when a later phase adds another space. The same aggregate-footprint check is missing for Falling Sky's alternate March shapes.
findings.prior_status: New confirmed normalization gap. Both origins/routes and alternate accepted plan representations reach the public human executor.
findings.disposition: Declared origins, explicit moves, extra groups, and routes produced by the planner obey the Limited Command and Britannia restrictions. Live validation precedes payment and movement after timing effects.

findings.title: Repeated Devastate Regions apply extra rounds of casualties in one Special Ability
findings.known_status: New confirmed extension of the repetition family. The original closed finding explicitly covered Seize and Entreat, and the Devastate repair covered casualty ownership and physical selection.
findings.expected: A Devastate Special Ability may select Carnutes only once and applies one casualty fraction there.
findings.observed: Raid Veneti with sa_regions [Carnutes, Carnutes] for Devastate is accepted as a durable human turn. Carnutes begins with Vercingetorix, 12 Arverni Warbands and 9 Roman Auxilia. It ends with 7 Warbands and 4 Auxilia after two reductions. The legal one-Region control leaves 9 Warbands and 6 Auxilia. Execution reports success and no errors.
findings.comparison: Liberty or Death coin-implementation-lessons.md §E records repeated Patriot Persuasion and Indian double-SA defects. Its per-Command once-only guard suggests checking every affected Region rather than relying on per-Region piece legality. Devastate may legally select an already Devastated Region on a later Command, so marker presence cannot enforce uniqueness within one execution.
findings.repair_scope: Validate unique selected Devastate Regions before mutation, using the same rule across before/after/during forms. Retain legal later-Command Devastation of an already marked Region.
findings.comparison_pattern: Liberty or Death coin-implementation-lessons.md §E records repeated Patriot Persuasion and Indian double-SA defects. Its per-Command once-only guard suggests checking every affected Region rather than relying on per-Region piece legality. Devastate may legally select an already Devastated Region on a later Command, so marker presence cannot enforce uniqueness within one execution.
findings.prior_status: New confirmed extension of the repetition family. The original closed finding explicitly covered Seize and Entreat, and the Devastate repair covered casualty ownership and physical selection.
findings.disposition: The human plan rejects repeated Devastate Regions before losses in before, during, and after timing. A legal single selection applies the casualty procedure once.

findings.title: Fort defense incorrectly restores Ambush saving rolls and suppresses Caesar’s test
findings.repro: PYTHONPATH=. python battle/probe_ambush.py (with the fs-bot checkout on PYTHONPATH)
findings.expected: A Fort halves the Attack Losses. Ambush still removes a piece for each resulting Loss without a saving roll. Caesar makes the printed exception test, and a successful test permits saving rolls and Counterattack.
findings.observed: An accepted Aedui Battle+Ambush with eight Warbands against three Roman Legions and a Fort inflicts two halved Losses but removes no Legions with seed0. With Caesar added, no Caesar test or Counterattack occurs. Both outcomes pass the board validator.
findings.known_status: The original inventory left BM-AMBUSH-FORT-SOURCE unverified. This audit promotes it to a confirmed mechanics defect. Existing tests encode the incorrect Fort interpretation.
findings.comparator: Liberty or Death docs/audit_set_but_never_applied_s76.md checks modifiers at their final observation point and traces parallel calculators. Here the Ambush rule is followed through the actual loss resolver and ordinary accepted Command. The supplied Falling Sky flowchart expressly makes the rules text authoritative.
findings.scope: Normal human Command+SA and shared Battle resolver. Fort cases executed; the same source branch also covers Citadels, but no separate Citadel witness is claimed.
findings.comparison_pattern: Liberty or Death docs/audit_set_but_never_applied_s76.md checks modifiers at their final observation point and traces parallel calculators. Here the Ambush rule is followed through the actual loss resolver and ordinary accepted Command. The supplied Falling Sky flowchart expressly makes the rules text authoritative.
findings.prior_status: The original inventory left BM-AMBUSH-FORT-SOURCE unverified. This audit promotes it to a confirmed mechanics defect. Existing tests encode the incorrect Fort interpretation.
findings.disposition: Fort and Citadel halving applies before automatic Ambush casualties. Defending Caesar tests even behind a Fort, with 5–6 required against Belgae. A successful test permits saving rolls and Counterattack. Base German Battle includes Ambush. Ordinary Ariovistus German Battle uses the usual defense.

limitations: Comparative source review and targeted witnesses, not an exhaustive state-space or 490-row recertification.
LoD provides engineering patterns. Supplied Falling Sky references and adopted rulings govern game behavior.
Two frontend witnesses use ordinary init/play/submit without editing state. Other witnesses use initialized or scenario-derived controlled positions and the stated public validators/executors.
Many malformed authored plans are rejected by terminal pickers but accepted by the durable/API route. No claim that terminal menus generate every bad input.
EX2-07 creates a structurally inconsistent final state. Starting expansion fixtures pass both pool/schema and structural checks.
Fifteen historical rows remain unverified; FE-NOPRUNING also retains a broad specialized-menu completeness uncertainty.
Previously recorded CV-PERSISTENCE and source questions are outside the new21 count.
No claim that all defects were introduced by recent repairs. Original50 dispositions retain their historical scope.
